statement: For degree d in the real projective plane, with r real points and (3d−1−r)/2 conjugate pairs in generic position, the signed rational-curve count χ_r^d=Σ_C(−1)^(solitary nodes of C) is independent of the configuration and |χ_r^d| bounds the ordinary real count below. Example 1 computes χ^3(T)=Σ_(j=0)^4 2jT^(2j); hence cubics through eight real points have at least eight real solutions.

answer.text: For degree d in the real projective plane, with r real points and (3d−1−r)/2 conjugate pairs in generic position, the signed rational-curve count χ_r^d=Σ_C(−1)^(solitary nodes of C) is independent of the configuration and |χ_r^d| bounds the ordinary real count below. Example 1 computes χ^3(T)=Σ_(j=0)^4 2jT^(2j); hence cubics through eight real points have at least eight real solutions.

scope: Real rational degree-d plane curves through a generic conjugation-invariant set of 3d−1 points, with a specified number of real points.
notes: Signed invariants are lower bounds, not the ordinary number of real curves. The article treats more general real symplectic four-manifolds; only the plane specialization is mapped here.
